question: Question linked to image nº25 A 60-year-old patient with a personal history of carcinoma of the lung presented with a two-week history of back pain and irradiated pain to the right arm and hand three days ago. MRI of the column shown in the image is performed. Given these clinical and radiological findings indicate the correct answer:

options.opa: Metastasis in the medullary cord with signs of expansion.
options.opb: Vertebral metastasis with pathological fracture that causes spinal cord compression.
options.opc: Vertebra in diabolo in the context of osteoporosis.
options.opd: Computed tomography is the "choice" image test in this pathology.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lung carcinoma -> potential for metastasis -> back pain and irradiated pain to the right arm and hand -> 70% CHAIN: Back pain and irradiated pain to the right arm and hand -> suggestive of spinal cord involvement -> MRI of the column performed -> 80% CHAIN: MRI findings show vertebral metastasis -> potential for pathological fracture -> spinal cord compression -> 85% CHAIN: Clinical and radiological findings consistent with vertebral metastasis -> likely cause of symptoms -> option B: Vertebral metastasis with pathological fracture that causes spinal cord compression -> 70%
analysis: The clinical history of a lung carcinoma patient with back pain and radiating pain to the arm, along with the MRI showing vertebral involvement, suggests a likely vertebral metastasis with possible spinal cord compression.
